khai.tagline: Social anxiety as process: the chronic fear of negative evaluation by others -- driven by anticipatory processing before social exposure, self-focused attention and the self as a social object during interaction, and post-event processing consolidating perceived failure (Clark & Wells; Rapee & Heimberg; Leary; Hofmann).

card.wire: Attaches at Process. The root (process_social_anxiety.md) models social anxiety as the chronic fear of negative evaluation by others: the perceived hazard is social scrutiny, rejection, or loss of standing, driven by a self-appraisal of inadequacy before an audience. Three movements carry the cycle: anticipatory processing, where the encounter is rehearsed and dreaded in advance; self-focused attention, where the persona monitors the self as a social object and deploys safety behaviors that prevent genuine contact; and post-event processing, where the finished interaction is reviewed through a biased lens that confirms the feared inadequacy.
card.issue: Three movements carry the maintenance loop. Anticipatory processing: the persona reviews the upcoming event, predicting humiliation and activating negative self-beliefs (Clark & Wells). Self-focused attention: during exposure, attention turns inward onto interoceptive sensations and an observer-perspective self-image, taking felt anxiety as evidence of visible failure (Rapee & Heimberg). Post-event processing: after leaving the situation, a ruminative post-mortem selects perceived flaws and cements the narrative of catastrophe, priming the next anticipatory cycle.
card.require: Two altitudes hold the engine. The law: declared once in the project's Instructions Knowledge chapter, linking the root, so the evaluative threat model governs wherever the engine is cast. The link, advisory: a persona holding a movement may link it under Projection, and the audit surfaces the ones left unnamed.
card.enforce: Structure is checked; coherence is judged. The kit verifies the floor: the law is declared and the engine's own members conform. Whether a production earns the read -- an ongoing surveillance of negative evaluation rather than acute embarrassment or general phobic fear -- is semantic, taught and reviewed, never failed by the suite. Hold the honest limit: social anxiety is character architecture for authoring, never a clinical assessment or diagnosis of a real person.
card.setup: Declare the law in the Instructions Knowledge chapter, linking the root. Stage the discrepancy between external social safety and internal catastrophic surveillance: the persona assumes the room is critical and monitoring, while the room is mostly indifferent or benign. Cast one or more movements deliberately: an encounter can be ruined days before it happens, crippled during by self-monitoring safety behaviors, or reconstructed into disaster hours afterward. Keep the boundaries: conditioned object-fear belongs to fear/phobia, acute transient mortification to embarrassment, and global self-defectiveness to shame -- this engine owns only the chronic fear of negative evaluation.
